findings.errorText: 文字数が正しくありません。
findings.guidanceRef: GovTech Tokyo Input Form Guidance ver 1.1, p.27 Name (氏名), item 3: set a sufficient maximum length, because foreign names need more characters
findings.observation: The single お名前 field kept the full 28-character name but showed the error 「文字数が正しくありません。」 (character count incorrect), and the form did not reach the confirmation screen. The baseline (山田 太郎) and shorter Latin names with spaces, up to 16 characters, all reached confirmation, so the rejection appears to come from length, not from spaces or Latin letters.
findings.relevance: Maria Clara Santos Dela Cruz is a common Filipino name with two given names and a compound family name, and anyone with such a name may need to contact this business. She cannot shorten her real name to fit the form.
findings.basis: This behaviour is inconsistent with the guidance on p.27, which asks for a sufficient maximum length because foreign names need more characters. The guidance is scoped to Tokyo Metropolitan Government forms, and this is a private site.
findings.cause: The rule was reproduced from behaviour, not confirmed in source: the input has no maxlength or pattern attribute, so a script or server-side check limits the character count. Passing and failing cases put the limit somewhere between 17 and 28 characters.
findings.fix: In the validation for flname, raise the maximum character count to a generous bound such as 100, and keep the required (non-empty) check and that upper bound so genuinely invalid input is still rejected. A fix verified on a local reproduction verifies the reproduction only, not the live site.

summary: 1 of 5 name cases stopped before the checkpoint; baseline reached_checkpoint.
